action.hypothesis:
Mechanism: deterministic self-consistency selector — majority vote over the 10 extracted candidate answers (Counter over non-None answers; tie -> earliest candidate index; all-None -> index 0). No AR features used.
Hypothesis: the seed's failure class is wrong credit assignment (candidate-level NLL instead of answer-level consensus); on dev, majority beats every AR selector by 15-45pts on the two dominant models (dream 0.235->0.700, llada 0.490->0.745) while the correct answer is present in 84.5-87.5% of their questions.
Observable: B_dev macro 0.148 -> ~0.29; per-model: dream-base ~0.70, llada-base ~0.745, floor models ~0-0.02 (unchanged).
Conflicts: none — attacks an axis no prior node touched.

insight: Plain majority vote (earliest-index tie-break, all-None -> 0) verified at B_dev macro 0.2940 (dream 0.7000, llada 0.7450, floors 0.000-0.015) — measured directly in both executors' comparison tables (nodes 2.1 and 3.1 each ran plain majority as their reference). Doubles the seed (0.148). The standalone pure-majority node was skipped at idea review, so no dedicated run; the score is established by the two independent executor evaluations of the identical core.

action.hypothesis: Mechanism: majority vote with an AR tie-break, using only this item's own 10 candidates. Rejected the cross-model cache: reading other models' answers to the same question is cross-model ensembling, which changes the task (one model's N samples), is unfair to every per-model baseline, and makes the score depend on evaluation order. Rule: count votes over extracted answers; among answers tied for the top count, pick the answer whose best candidate has the lowest per-token NLL (nll_sum / n_tokens) under qwen7b; earliest index as the last resort; all-None -> 0. Hypothesis: ties are where majority vote loses most, and per-token NLL from the strongest scorer may separate tied answers even though it is anti-predictive across all candidates. Observable: dream-base and llada-base dev >= majority (0.700 / 0.745); if not, report that AR likelihood adds nothing on top of the vote.

insight:
AR-likelihood tie-breaking is not useful here. When vote counts tie, using qwen7b per-token NLL to select among tied answers does not improve accuracy; it is roughly neutral to anti-predictive. The method helps only in a narrow subset where the base model is already strong, while elsewhere it flips correct answers as often as it fixes wrong ones. Plain majority vote remains safer. Actionable conclusion: do not use raw AR NLL as a self-consistency tie-breaker for these per-item, closed-model comparisons. Future tie-breakers should use signals better aligned with answer correctness, such as calibrated answer probability, semantic similarity, uncertainty, or external verifier evidence.
[Pruned: Verified negative on B_dev (node 2.1, 0.2900 < 0.294 majority core): qwen7b per-token NLL tie-breaking resolved 27 dream ties but was net -5 items (1 fix vs 6 breaks); llada net 0 (4/4). The anti-predictiveness of per-token NLL survives restriction to tied answers — NLL measures fluency/length artifacts, not correctness. No recovery path within the tie-break axis.]

action.hypothesis: Mechanism: likelihood-weighted voting, run as a falsification test of the brief's direction. Score each distinct extracted answer by the sum over its candidates of exp(-per-token NLL) and pick the highest (tie -> earliest candidate; all-None -> 0). Scorer per model: dream-base -> qwen7b (its own AR base), diffullama -> llama2-7b (its own AR base), every other model -> qwen7b. Correction to the proposal: LLaDA has no AR base model; it is the control, so do not call llama2-7b its base. Hypothesis: dev diagnostics predict per-token NLL does not add information as a vote weight (correct minority has lower NLL than the plurality in only 2/14 dream and 8/18 llada dev cases); this node turns that into a recorded result. Observable: B_dev macro below the pure-majority node -> prune and record the negative; >= majority -> keep and refine. Report per-model dev scores.

insight:
Using AR per-token NLL as a vote weight did not improve answer selection and was often counterproductive. In decisive cases, NLL acted as an anti-predictor: it favored fluent but incorrect minority responses over correct majority answers. The signal appears to track surface-level fluency, length, and stylistic artifacts rather than factual correctness.

Actionable conclusion: do not use raw per-token likelihood as a confidence or vote-weighting mechanism for candidate answers. Plain majority voting is stronger and simpler in this setting. Future work should treat likelihood weighting as failed unless re-calibrated against correctness, or replace it with more discriminative signals such as calibrated confidence, answer-agreement metrics, or error-aware scoring that penalizes fluent-but-wrong candidates.
[Pruned: Verified negative on B_dev (node 3.1, 0.2820): likelihood-weighted voting (sum exp(-per-token NLL) per answer, own-base scorer) scored 0.650/0.730 vs 0.700/0.745 majority on dream/llada. In the decisive cases the correct minority has lower NLL than the plurality in only 2/14 dev-dream and 8/18 dev-llada — at/below chance, so weights systematically flip plausibility-correct majorities to fluent-wrong minorities. The brief's proposed mechanism is audited dead; per-token NLL captures fluency, not correctness.]

action.hypothesis:
Mechanism: majority vote with qwen7b per-token NLL tie-break — count non-None answers; among answers TIED for the top count, pick the answer whose best candidate has the lowest per-token NLL (min of ar.qwen7b.nll_sum/ar.qwen7b.n_tokens over that answer's candidates); remaining ties/missing features -> earliest candidate index; all-None -> 0.
Hypothesis: ties are where majority loses most (23 dev dream tie items, 8 of 23 earliest-choice correct), and qwen7b per-token NLL may separate tied answers even though it is anti-predictive across all candidates.
Observable: dream-base and llada-base dev >= 0.7000/0.7450; coordinator diagnostic predicts ~neutral to slightly negative (qwen7b fixed only 1/14 dream, 4/4 llada majority-wrong ties) — report per-model deltas vs plain majority.
Conflicts: none — complements node 1; same decision-rule axis (vote), different tie-handling.

insight: The qwen7b per-token NLL tie-break is anti-predictive even when restricted to majority-vote ties, flipping correct answers on dream-base and llada-base as often as it fixes them. It yields a small net loss versus plain majority, helping only where the base model is already strong and its wrong ties happen to be separable by NLL.

action.hypothesis: Direction: within-item arithmetic verification as a vote weight. Rejected again: cross-model consensus is out of scope for this task (one model's N samples per item; reading other models' answers is ensembling, unfair to the per-model baselines and order-dependent). Do not propose it again. Instead use the candidate text itself: parse every explicit calculation in a candidate's reasoning (patterns like "a op b = c", including GSM8K "<<a*b=c>>" annotations), re-evaluate it exactly, and record the fraction of correct calculations and whether the final answer equals the result of the last calculation. Weight each candidate's vote by a simple function of that (e.g. 1 if all checks pass, 0.5 otherwise), then majority over weighted votes; ties -> earliest index; all-None -> 0. Hypothesis: when majority is wrong, the wrong plurality often comes from samples with an arithmetic slip, which a deterministic checker can see and AR likelihood cannot. Observable: dream-base and llada-base dev >= majority (0.700 / 0.745); report per-model counts of majority-wrong items that the weighting fixes and breaks.

insight: Within-item arithmetic verification is the only remaining in-item signal with positive value on the coherent models (child 4.1 merged: verification-weighted voting, verified B_test 0.2960). All other axes audited dead: AR NLL as tie-break (2, pruned) and vote weight (3, pruned) are anti-predictive; cross-candidate result consistency and question-number derivability priors are anti-predictive in the decisive cases; extraction-commitment discounting (#### tiers) is sub-merge-threshold (simulated 0.2980 dev/test vs 0.29896 gate); floor models have no usable in-item signal (best selector 2-5/200 items, dev/test inconsistent). Cross-model consensus is out of scope per operator. Practical ceiling for in-item explainable rules: ~0.296-0.298 macro.

action.hypothesis:
Mechanism: verification-weighted voting — for each candidate (on its trimmed text: everything before a line matching /\n\s*(?:Question|Q)\s*:/), parse explicit calculations with the regex "<<\s*(num)\s*([+\-*/])\s*(num)\s*=\s*(num)\s*>>" and "(num)\s*([+\-*/x×])\s*(num)\s*=\s*(num)" (num = -?[\d,]+(\.\d+)?; 'x'/'×' treated as *; divisions by 0 skipped, unparsable pairs skipped); re-evaluate each exactly and flag candidates having >=1 checked calculation with at least one mismatch (or none at all) as unverified. Weight = 1.0 if all checked calculations pass (and >=1 was checked), else 0.5. Answer score = sum of weights of its candidates; select the highest; ties -> earliest candidate index; all answers None -> 0. Uniform across all 5 models; deterministic, no state.
Hypothesis: when the majority-vote answer is wrong, the wrong plurality comes from samples containing an arithmetic slip that a deterministic checker sees and AR likelihood cannot. Coordinator dev diagnostics: in the 29 dream majority-wrong cases the correct candidate has all-passing calcs 9x vs 4x for the plurality (and last-calc==answer 11 vs 8); expected dream dev ~0.715 (+3 items). LLaDA shows the OPPOSITE pattern (correct all-pass 4/26 vs plurality 8/26) so expect llada dev ~0.740 (-1 item); net macro ~0.296 > 0.294 majority.
Observable: B_dev macro >= 0.295 with dream-base ~0.710-0.720; per-model report incl. floor models. If dream < 0.705 the mechanism is dead -> prune.
Conflicts: none — new evidence axis (in-item arithmetic consistency); orthogonal to the pruned AR-NLL axes (2, 3).

insight: MERGED (verified B_test 0.2960, up from 0.157 baseline). Verification-weighted voting: majority vote over extracted answers, candidate weight 1.0 if all its explicit calculations re-evaluate correctly (>=1 checked) else 0.5; answer score = sum of weights; ties -> earliest. Dev 0.296 (dream 0.715 = +3 fixes/0 breaks, llada 0.740 = 1 fix/2 breaks). Test 0.296 (dream 0.725, llada 0.720, floors 0.005-0.02). In-item arithmetic consistency is a real, if modest, signal on the coherent models; floors have ~no calculations and are untouched.
